title: Nib's Perfect Pet
markdown:
Nib the goblin had a super-duper important wish! It was more important than finding the sparkliest pebble or the yummiest berry. Nib wanted a pet! He lived way up high on the windy Sunspike Peaks. The air there whistled fun tunes through the rocky cliffs, and the clouds sometimes tickled his pointy ears. His home was cosy, with piles and piles of soft mossy cushions and glow-worm lanterns that made a warm, gentle light. But, oh dearie me, it felt a little bit lonely. Nib really, really wished for a furry, or maybe scaly, or even feathery friend to share his adventures!

“A pet!” he declared one blustery morning, his bright green nose wiggling with pure excitement. The wind ruffled his spiky hair, making him feel ready for anything. “I need a pet!”

With a hop, skip, and a bounce, he scurried down to the Whispering Woods. His friends there were always happy to chat and share their funny ideas. First, he met Pipkin the Pixie. Pipkin zipped all around Nib’s head like a speedy, sparkly bumblebee. Pipkin’s wings sparkled with every color of the rainbow, leaving little trails of glitter in the air.

“A pet, Nib? Oh, how absolutely thrilling!” Pipkin giggled. Her voice sounded like tiny bells tinkling. “You should get a cloud-kitten! They float and purr like fluffy marshmallows, and they taste like sunshine on a warm day!”

Nib imagined a fluffy cloud purring right on his lap. Its fur would be as soft as dandelion fluff. “But… how do you catch a cloud-kitten, Pipkin?” he asked, his eyebrows knitting together in confusion. They seemed so very high up!

Pipkin just winked, a mischievous sparkle in her eye. “That’s part of the fun, Nib! You’ll have to be quick and clever!”

Next, Nib shuffled along a winding path, his boots making a crunchy sound on the fallen leaves. He went to find Bramble the Badger. Bramble was quietly sniffing a patch of nice-smelling thyme, his whiskers wiggling. Bramble’s voice was a low, comforting rumble, like far-off thunder on a warm evening.

“A pet, you say? That’s a very good idea, Nib,” Bramble said, giving a slow, thoughtful nod. “I’d suggest a rock-biter. They’re very quiet, you see, and they’re super good at polishing stones. You’d always have the shiniest pebbles in the whole valley!”

Nib pictured a tiny creature with sharp teeth nibbling on rocks. It sounded… a bit dusty. He wasn't sure his cosy home would like all that rock dust. “But… what if it nibbled my favourite mossy cushion, Bramble?” he worried, imagining little toothy marks.

Bramble stroked his chin whiskers. “Hmm, that’s a very good point, Nib. Indeed. Perhaps a very small, very well-behaved burrow-owl then? They keep the mice away, you know.”

Nib was starting to feel a bit dizzy. His head was spinning faster than Pipkin’s wings! Cloud-kittens that tasted like sunshine and rock-biters that polished stones! It was all so… confusing! Just then, a huge shadow fell over the trees. Nib jumped! It was Ignis the Dragon, his amazing emerald scales glinting like a thousand jewels in the dappled sunlight. Ignis was known everywhere for his loud voice and his even louder, and often bonkers, ideas.

“Ho there, little goblin!” Ignis boomed. His voice rattled the leaves on the trees like they were maracas! “Heard you’re looking for a friend! Well, step right up! I have just the thing! A fire-lizard! They breathe little puffs of smoke – perfect for warming your toes on chilly nights!”

Nib imagined a tiny lizard breathing little puffs of smoke right into his cosy home. “But… what if it sets my glow-worm lanterns on fire, Mr. Ignis?” he whispered, his eyes wide with wonder and worry. He loved his glow-worm lanterns!

Ignis let out a great puff of smoke that smelled a little like burnt toast and adventure. “Nonsense! A tiny spark, that’s all! Perfectly safe! Or, if that’s not exciting enough, perhaps a grumpy griffin cub! They’re excellent at guarding things. No one would dare steal your berries if a griffin was on watch!”

Nib gulped. A little lump formed in his throat. A grumpy griffin? He imagined tiny, sharp claws and a very loud, very grumpy squawk that would scare away all the friendly woodland creatures. He felt a wobbly feeling in his knees, the kind that always appeared when he had to make a big choice. He was supposed to be choosing a pet, a friend, but all the advice was making his head feel like a tangled ball of yarn, all knots and no end. He thanked his friends very politely, his voice a little shaky. He wandered off, feeling a bit sad and very, very unsure.

He found himself on a high, windswept ledge looking out over the big, green valley. The wind tugged at his ears and his spiky hair, making him feel even smaller. He sat down with a big sigh, pulling his knees to his chest. His bright green nose drooped a little. He felt like a lost mushroom, all alone and a bit soggy. He wasn't brave enough for cloud-kittens. He worried too much about dust from rock-biters. And he was definitely not ready for grumpy griffins and their noisy squawks.

As he sat there, feeling sorry for himself, a tiny, soft sound caught his ear. It was a delicate, fluttering sound, like leaves dancing in the breeze. He slowly peeked over the edge of the ledge. On a little rocky spot, tucked amongst the grey stones, was something very small and very fluffy. It had ears that looked like delicate green leaves, so perfectly shaped. Its eyes were like two shiny black pebbles, bright and watching everything. It shivered a little in the strong wind, looking a bit lost and a bit lonely.

Nib’s heart did a little flutter, a happy, hopeful flip. This creature wasn’t a cloud-kitten, or a rock-biter, or a fiery lizard. It was just… small. And quiet. And it looked a little bit scared, just like he felt sometimes when he had to make big choices.

Very, very slowly, Nib held out a finger. His hand trembled just a little. The little creature tilted its leaf-like head. Its pebble eyes watched him curiously. Then, it took a hesitant step forward. Its tiny paws made no sound on the rock. It sniffed his finger with its tiny, wet nose. It felt warm and surprisingly soft against his skin. Then, it let out a tiny, happy squeak, a sound so sweet it made Nib smile.

Nib smiled. A big, wide, toothy goblin smile that stretched all the way to his pointy ears. This little creature didn’t need loud advice from dragons, or silly ideas from pixies, or even sensible suggestions from badgers. It just needed a friend. He gently scooped it up into his hands. It snuggled into his palms right away, its leaf-ears twitching happily.

He decided to call it Flicker, because its gentle spirit seemed to flicker with a soft, warm light. As he carried Flicker home, the wind didn’t seem so lonely anymore. The rocky cliffs didn’t seem so scary. He wasn't worried about cloud-kittens or grumpy griffin cubs. He had found his own special pet, his own perfect friend, and it was absolutely wonderful.

Back in his cosy home, Flicker explored the mossy cushions with curious little hops. Its leaf-ears perked up and looked around. Nib watched, his heart feeling warm and full, like a freshly baked berry pie. He hadn't needed any big plans or loud advice. He just needed to be quiet, and to look, and to be kind. And that, Nib realised with a happy sigh, was the bravest adventure of all. His home finally felt complete, filled with the soft chirping sounds of Flicker and the gentle, warm glow of a friendship he had found all by himself.
